analysis.title: GS Sharkey - US Equities Mid Day Color 5 Nov 2026
key_insights: The session fully reversed yesterday's relief rally and matched the initial futures reaction to the Midterm results. Mag7 (GSX1MEGA) fell 400bps, its second biggest move lower this year, and yesterday's demand was short lived.
The AI trade is under extreme pressure: Neoclouds (GSXUNEOC) -14%, Memory (GSTMTMEM) -12%, AI (GSTMTAIP) -8%. Semis fell 9% and are driving the negative price loop.
SOX is down 35% from its local highs, the third largest peak to trough selloff in the past 3 years. NVDA is now negative on the year.

Hedge fund VIP vs VIP Short (GSTHVIPP) fell 200bps as positioning pressure and leverage unwind force funds to sell into weakness. Fundamental TMT long/short books were -382bps as of 10:30 EST. Systematics was the only strategy positive on the day, +51bps.
Market volumes are +32% vs yesterday and +57% vs the YTD average. Top of Book liquidity of $3.8mm is down 65% vs the YTD average, which exacerbates moves.
ETFs are 34% of volume (highest since April) and retail is selling. GS reads this as top-down pressure applied through macro instruments. SPY volume is +160% vs 20d, QQQ +100%, SMH +150%, DRAM +75%.

TMT: the AI trade is under extreme pressure for a second day after the midterms and is leaking into broader tech (NDX -5.5%). Hyperscalers are lower and cannot support the index. GS flows show minimal defense, but market supply looks top-down and indiscriminate via index, ETF, basket and macro products.

Healthcare is balanced in aggregate but bifurcated. Biotech and tools see broad supply (about -1.9 buy/sell skew), while large pharma and the index level see demand through systematic rotation (SMH -10%). Medtech was defensive again.

Financials: tech weakness (QQQ) again coincided with Financials strength (XLF), but less broadly than yesterday. Alts, IBs, Trads and Fintech did not participate. Insurance (KIE) leads, as it has through a 12% QTD rally.

Consumer: retail outperforms by less than yesterday on weaker overnight restaurant prints and soft off-price checks. HD/LOW strength continues, with questions on TSCO outperformance. Off-price stocks are only modestly down because soft end-3Q checks are somewhat known and likely weather and rotation driven.

Industrials: the risk-off tone is more aggressive than yesterday. Industrials -165bps, materials -100bps, broader markets -200bps. Utilities lead, tech lags, agriculture is up and data center names are hit hard.

GS flows do not match price action in intensity: 5/10 with a -8% sell skew. Long onlies and hedge funds are both 10% better for sale. Info Tech was net sold $1.4bn, the 6th straight session of selling and net selling in 4 of the last 5 weeks. Comm Services are 14% better for sale, the opposite of yesterday.
GS has net sold $27bn of Tech (Info Tech + Comm Services) since the start of this unwind, exceeding the $21bn net sold in the July unwind.
Chart of the Day: SOX is 14% below its 200dma (10,826) and 38% from its local highs, and the GS desk continues to see supply.

sector_views.rationale: AI, semis, memory and neocloud baskets are under heavy selling. GS flows have net sold $27bn of Tech since the unwind began and the desk continues to see supply in semis.
Balanced in aggregate but bifurcated. Biotech and tools see supply, large pharma sees demand, and medtech is defensive.
Financials are getting a bid from tech weakness, led by insurance (KIE), but participation is narrower than yesterday. Alts, IBs, Trads and Fintech are not participating.
Retail outperforms less than yesterday after weak restaurant prints and soft off-price checks. HD/LOW remain strong.
Risk-off tone is more aggressive. Industrials -165bps, materials -100bps, utilities leading, data center names hit hard.

risk_factors: Further forced selling by levered hedge funds in TMT as positioning pressure and leverage unwind.
Thin liquidity (Top of Book -65% vs YTD average) amplifies price moves.
Top-down, indiscriminate supply via ETFs, index and macro products.
Weakness in semis feeding a negative price action loop into broader tech and hyperscalers.
